description: How money moves electronically: payment systems, clearing and settlement, cards and online payments, the architecture of mobile money platforms, agent networks, USSD and app channels, interoperability between providers, and fraud and consumer protection, with Ghana's GhIPSS and mobile money market as the running case. Students design and simulate a working mobile money system in the browser, posting every transaction to a double-entry ledger and tracing it through the switch, the agent and the USSD menu.
modelledOn: CPMI-IOSCO, Principles for Financial Market Infrastructures
ISO 20022 and ISO 8583 financial messaging standards
PCI DSS (Payment Card Industry Data Security Standard)
GSMA Mobile Money API specification and Mobile Money Certification
outcomes: Explain how payment systems clear and settle transactions and compare gross and net settlement and their risks.
Describe the card and online payment flows, their message standards and the security controls that protect them.
Design the architecture of a mobile money platform, including wallets, a double-entry ledger, the trust account and its APIs.
Analyse agent network operations, including float, liquidity and commissions, and USSD and app channel design.
Explain how interoperability between providers is achieved through a national switch and how disputes and reversals are handled.
Identify common payment fraud and evaluate controls, KYC tiers and consumer protection rules set by regulators.

units.title: Money, payments and payment systems
topics: Functions of money; cash, central bank money, commercial bank money and e-money
Payment instruments: cash, cheques, credit transfers, direct debits, cards, mobile money and QR payments
Parties in a payment: payer, payee, their providers, the switch or scheme, the settlement agent and the regulator
The payments landscape in Ghana and Africa: the Bank of Ghana, GhIPSS, banks, electronic money issuers and fintechs
Financial inclusion: why mobile money spread in Africa, from M-Pesa in Kenya to Ghana's mobile money market

units.title: Payment systems and clearing
topics: Clearing and settlement: authorisation, clearing, netting and settlement; finality and irrevocability
Real-time gross settlement (the Ghana Interbank Settlement system) versus deferred net settlement (ACH)
Cheque codeline clearing, ACH direct credits and debits, and instant payment systems such as GhIPSS Instant Pay
Settlement risk, liquidity risk and credit risk; collateral, prefunding and intraday liquidity
Payment messages: ISO 20022 structure (pacs, pain and camt messages) and migration from legacy formats
Simulating netting across banks and computing settlement positions

units.title: Cards and online payments
topics: Card schemes and the four-party model: issuer, acquirer, scheme, merchant and cardholder; interchange and the merchant discount rate
Card transaction flow: authorisation, clearing and settlement; ISO 8583 messages and response codes
Chip cards and EMV: cryptograms, offline and online authentication; contactless payment
Online payments: payment gateways, 3-D Secure, tokenisation, chargebacks and card-not-present fraud
PCI DSS requirements and reducing scope with hosted payment pages and tokens
National card schemes such as gh-link and regional switching

units.title: Mobile money architecture
topics: The mobile money model: electronic money issuer, trust account at a bank, e-value backed one-to-one by funds
Platform architecture: wallet service, double-entry ledger, transaction engine, fees and limits, notification service
Transaction types: cash-in, cash-out, person-to-person transfer, merchant payment, bill payment, bulk disbursement
Correctness under failure: atomic transactions, idempotency keys, reconciliation and handling timeouts
APIs for merchants and partners; the GSMA Mobile Money API and callback design
Regulation: the Payment Systems and Services Act 2019 (Act 987), licence categories and trust account rules

units.title: Agent networks
topics: The role of agents: cash-in and cash-out points that turn e-value into cash and back
Agent hierarchy: master agents, sub-agents and merchants; recruitment, training and supervision
Liquidity management: e-float and cash float, rebalancing, and running out of float on market days
Commission structures, agent economics and the viability of rural agents
Agent fraud and errors: split transactions, unauthorised withdrawals, and agent monitoring
Simulating an agent network and the float rebalancing across a district

units.title: USSD and app channels
topics: USSD as a channel: sessions, shortcodes, menu trees, session timeouts and USSD gateway integration
Designing USSD menus for low literacy and feature phones: menu depth, confirmations, PIN entry and local languages
Smartphone apps, SIM toolkit applications and their security trade-offs
QR code payments and interoperable QR (GhQR); NFC and the move to merchant acceptance
Building and usability-testing a USSD mobile money menu in the browser simulator

units.title: Interoperability between providers
topics: Closed-loop versus interoperable systems; bilateral links versus a central switch
The GhIPSS Mobile Money Interoperability platform: wallet-to-wallet and wallet-to-bank transfers
Switch design: routing, name enquiry, transaction status queries, reversals and dispute resolution
Settlement between providers: net positions, settlement windows and reconciliation files
Cross-border payments and remittances: corridors, correspondent banking and the Pan-African Payment and Settlement System (PAPSS)
Interoperability elsewhere in Africa: Tanzania, Kenya, Rwanda and the WAEMU zone compared

units.title: Fraud and consumer protection
topics: Common mobile money fraud: social engineering, fake reversal requests, SIM swap, PIN theft and insider fraud
Fraud detection: velocity rules, device and location signals, anomaly detection and case management
Customer due diligence and KYC tiers with the Ghana Card; transaction and balance limits
Consumer protection: transparent fees, complaint handling, dispute timelines and dormant accounts
Taxes and levies on electronic transfers and their effect on usage

units.title: The future of payments and capstone
topics: Central bank digital currencies: the eCedi pilot, design choices and offline payments
Open banking and payment APIs; super-apps and embedded finance
Savings and credit on mobile money: digital susu, nano-loans and their risks
Capstone: design and simulate an interoperable mobile money service with a USSD menu, a ledger, agents and settlement through a switch

schedule.title: Money, payment instruments and the Ghana landscape
schedule.exercise: Map one everyday payment (buying airtime by mobile money) onto the parties, instrument and regulator involved, and write a one-page summary of why mobile money spread in Africa.

tasks.title: Classify ten payment scenarios by instrument (cash, card, transfer, mobile money, QR) and choose the cheapest suitable one for each stated need
Trace a card purchase and a mobile money merchant payment, naming each party and the money or message they pass, and score the completed trace
Advise a rural trader on whether to adopt mobile money, weighing cost, trust, agent access and cash needs, and defend the recommendation to a rubric

schedule.title: Clearing and settlement
schedule.exercise: Explain with a worked numeric example the difference between real-time gross settlement and deferred net settlement, and which costs more liquidity.

tasks.title: Follow a transfer through authorisation, clearing and settlement in a branching case and decide at which point the payment becomes final
Store a day of interbank transfers in tables and compute each bank's multilateral net position with a SQL query, then check that positions sum to zero
Choose between cheque clearing, ACH and instant payment for four business cases and justify each choice against cost, speed and risk

schedule.title: Settlement risk and payment messages
schedule.exercise: Read an ISO 20022 credit transfer message and label each element with its meaning, then write what a legacy field would map to.

tasks.title: Parse a sample payment message stored as rows of fields, extract payer, payee, amount and reference, and flag one invalid message
Simulate netting among five banks over a day's payments and compute the settlement amounts, then confirm bilateral and multilateral netting reduce volumes
Handle a scenario in which one bank cannot fund its net position at settlement time, choose among prefunding, collateral and delay, and defend the choice

schedule.title: Card payments
schedule.exercise: Draw the four-party card model with the money flows for a 100 cedi purchase, including interchange and the merchant discount rate, and compute each party's share.

tasks.title: Calculate interchange, scheme fee and merchant discount for 20 card sales using a fee table in the database, and check the totals reconcile
Walk through an authorisation request and response, interpret three response codes and decide the right customer message for each
Investigate a disputed contactless transaction using chip cryptogram and terminal evidence, and decide who bears the loss under the scheme rules

schedule.title: Online card payments and standards
schedule.exercise: Write a checklist a small online shop could use to reduce its PCI DSS scope by using a hosted payment page and tokens.

tasks.title: Handle a chargeback case for a card-not-present purchase by gathering the right evidence and choosing to accept or contest it
Evaluate three shop designs (stores card numbers, uses hosted page, uses tokens) for PCI scope and rank them with reasons
Plan how a new bank should join a national card scheme and switch, picking connection, certification and testing steps in order against a rubric

schedule.title: The mobile money model and platform
schedule.exercise: Explain with an example why every unit of e-money must be backed one-to-one by funds in a trust account, and what would go wrong otherwise.

tasks.title: Model wallets and a trust account in tables, perform a cash-in and cash-out and check that total e-money equals the trust balance after each step
Design a double-entry ledger for a person-to-person transfer with a fee, run it as a SQL transaction and show debits equal credits
Add merchant payment, bill payment and bulk disbursement flows to the ledger and verify the fee and settlement accounts balance for 100 test transactions

schedule.title: Correctness, APIs and regulation
schedule.exercise: Summarise the main licence categories and trust account rules under Act 987 in a one-page table for a start-up, with the obligations of each.

tasks.title: Show with two simulated transfers how a retried request without an idempotency key double-charges a customer and then fix it with a key
Reconcile a provider ledger against a partner statement after a timeout, find three mismatched entries and decide whether to reverse, confirm or investigate each
Decide which licence a proposed service needs and which trust account rules apply, in a branching case scored against a compliance rubric

schedule.title: Agent networks and liquidity
schedule.exercise: Calculate the daily commission and float needs for a rural agent on a market day and argue whether the agent is viable.

tasks.title: Track an agent's e-float and cash float through 30 transactions in tables and show when the agent must rebalance to avoid running out
Compute commission income and costs for three agents with different volumes and find the break-even number of transactions per day
Manage float rebalancing for a district of eight agents across a week with market-day spikes and score the plan on stock-outs avoided and rebalancing cost

schedule.title: USSD design and usability
schedule.exercise: Sketch a USSD menu tree for sending money and paying a bill, then test it on a classmate and note every point where they hesitated.

tasks.title: Map the screens of a five-step USSD session, set the session timeout and decide what happens to a transaction if the session drops midway
Redesign a four-level USSD menu so a first-time user finishes a transfer in fewer steps, with confirmation and PIN screens, and justify each change
Build a USSD menu in the browser simulator with balance, send money and bill payment, then test twelve paths including wrong PIN and timeout

schedule.title: Interoperability and the switch
schedule.exercise: Compare bilateral links with a central switch for connecting five providers, counting links needed and the cost of adding a sixth.

tasks.title: Choose between bilateral integration and a central switch for a group of five providers and justify the choice on cost, time and risk
Route 30 wallet-to-wallet and wallet-to-bank transfers through a switch table by destination prefix and report any that fail with the reason
Resolve a failed interoperable transfer where the sender was debited and the receiver not credited, using status queries and reversals, scored on the dispute rubric

schedule.title: Settlement between providers and cross-border payments
schedule.exercise: Compare PAPSS with correspondent banking for a Ghana to Nigeria remittance in cost, speed and number of intermediaries.

tasks.title: Produce a settlement file of net positions between three providers from a day of interoperable transfers and check it against each provider's records
Select the cheapest and fastest route for sending 500 dollars from Accra to Lagos from three corridor options and defend the choice with fees
Find reconciliation breaks between two providers' settlement files for a week, classify the causes and propose fixes that prevent recurrence

schedule.title: Fraud, KYC, consumer protection and tax
schedule.exercise: Write a consumer awareness leaflet that explains five common mobile money scams and what a customer should do after each.

tasks.title: Respond to a customer who has been tricked by a fake reversal request, deciding what to block, whom to inform and how to explain it
Write SQL rules for velocity and amount thresholds that flag suspicious wallets in a transaction table, and measure how many true cases they catch
Decide which KYC tier and limits apply to five customer profiles, and handle an application with a mismatched Ghana Card number

schedule.title: Digital currencies, open finance and capstone
schedule.exercise: Write a design brief for an interoperable mobile money service describing its users, ledger, agent model, USSD menu, switch connection and settlement.

tasks.title: Assess a digital susu and nano-loan product for a trader, spotting the risks of over-borrowing and high charges, and rate it on a consumer rubric
Compare an eCedi pilot with mobile money for an offline payment scenario in a remote market, and recommend which fits better with reasons
Build the capstone ledger, agent float and switch settlement tables, run 100 transactions across two providers and show all balances reconcile
